draft.title: Entrepreneurship and innovation
card: a person who sees an opportunity and takes on the risk of starting a business to act on it. They may lose the money and time they put in.
a new or better product, or a new or better way of working. It can be a new invention or an improvement to something that already exists.
A business that innovates may offer something customers prefer, so it can win sales from rivals.
Rivals then respond with their own improvements or lower prices. In this way innovation drives competition between businesses.
draft.remember: Entrepreneurs take the risk of starting. Innovation pushes businesses to compete.

a.q: Which person is acting as an entrepreneur?
opts: Tom, who spots a gap and risks his savings on a bike shop
Priya, who is paid a wage to fix bikes at a shop she works in
Sam, who buys a bike from a shop to ride to work each day
Lee, who reads about bike shops for a school assignment
a.why: Tom sees an opportunity and takes on the risk of starting a business. Priya works in a business but does not carry the risk of starting it, which is the tempting wrong answer.
a.clue: Look for the person who starts the business and carries the risk.

b.q: Ava's bakery in Bathurst begins selling bread made with a new method that keeps it fresh for longer. Rival bakeries then improve their own bread. Which idea does this show?
opts: Profit being the reward for taking a risk
A business causing harm to quality of life
A business selling goods instead of services
b.why: Ava's new method is an innovation, and the rivals respond by improving their own products. That is competition driven by innovation. Profit is not the best answer because the case is about how rivals respond, not about what Ava earns.
b.clue: Focus on what the rival bakeries did after Ava's change.
